This model examines the cross-sectional association between age and spoken words in typically developing children, extending VG03 with dataset and child random intercepts to account for between-lab variation and repeated Wordbank administrations.

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
```

## Statistical model

We model the number of words spoken as a bounded count outcome out of an 810-word reference inventory. The expected proportion of words spoken is modelled as a smooth function of age. On the logit scale, this function is the sum of a linear developmental trend, a Gaussian process term anchored at 19 months, a dataset intercept, and a child intercept. Both random-effect blocks use non-centred Normal parameterisations. Population-level means set the random effects to zero; predictive count trajectories sample one new-child intercept per posterior draw. A Beta-Binomial likelihood with age-varying dispersion accounts for residual extra-binomial variation. Wordbank WG, Oxford CDI, and Words & Sentences rows contribute spoken observations, and a fixed-seed sensitivity retains one administration per child.

::: {.callout-note title="Model at a glance"}

- **Population:** typically developing children.
- **Outcome:** words spoken out of the common 810-word reference inventory.
- **Data handling:** full TD data rather than the VG03 subsample; datasets with fewer than 200 observations are filtered.
- **Hierarchy:** dataset and child random intercepts; one-administration-per-child sensitivity.
- **Stabilisation:** the GP is anchored at 19 months.

:::

::: {.callout-note}

For full details and discussion, please refer to the technical report.

## Priors

The trajectory priors match the TD spoken baseline anchors at 12 and 26 months. The dataset and child random-effect scales each use a HalfNormal(0.5) prior on the logit scale. The 19-month GP anchor is a stabilisation constraint that separates the GP level from the intercept and random effects; it is not a substantive claim that development changes uniquely at 19 months.

## Posterior predictions

The main findings to inspect are how the full-data, study-adjusted spoken trajectory differs from VG03, and whether the study random effects reduce uncertainty or reveal between-dataset heterogeneity.

### Posterior summary table for selected ages

In this model, $p$ is the latent success probability -- the underlying proportion of the vocabulary checklist a child is expected to produce at a given age. $Ey$ is the expected value implied by the latent mean $p$. It reflects uncertainty in the mean developmental trajectory. $Y$ is a draw from the posterior predictive distribution. It reflects both uncertainty in the mean trajectory and extra-binomial variability (dispersion).

```{python}
posterior_summary = pd.read_csv("posterior_summary.csv", index_col=0)
posterior_summary
```

### Posterior predictive probability mass function (PMF) for word counts, by age

The probability of observing a specific count of words spoken for selected ages.

![posterior_predictive_pmf](posterior_predictive_pmf.png){#fig-posterior-predictive-pmf .lightbox fig-align="left"}

### Posterior predictive cumulative distribution function (CDF) for word counts, by age

The cumulative sum of the PMF: the probability that the count of words spoken is less than or equal to a specified value for selected ages.

![posterior_predictive_cdf](posterior_predictive_cdf.png){#fig-posterior-predictive-cdf .lightbox fig-align="left"}

### Cross-sectional age derivative

The posterior distribution of the derivative of expected spoken words with respect to age, in words per month. This is a cross-sectional derivative of the fitted population trajectory, not a within-child learning rate.

![expected_learning_rate](expected_learning_rate.png){#fig-expected-learning-rate .lightbox fig-align="left"}

### Posterior distribution for dispersion parameter $\kappa$

Lower $\kappa$ values indicate greater overdispersion (greater between-child variability relative to the mean), while higher $\kappa$ values indicate less overdispersion (less between-child variability relative to the mean).

![posterior_kappa](posterior_kappa.png){#fig-posterior-kappa .lightbox fig-align="left"}
